name: func_01ff8df8

floor.evidence: ROUTING FLOOR, not a codegen wall -- there is no original C to recover, so no amount of matching effort can succeed. 0x01ff8000..0x01ffb07c is vendor runtime: CodeWarrior's soft-float library plus its integer division helpers. Measured, not assumed: compiling a/b, a%b and ua/ub at 1.2/sp2p3 with repo flags leaves undefined references to _s32_div_f and _u32_div_f, and % lowers to `bl _s32_div_f; mov r0,r1` -- so 0x01ffabe4 and 0x01ffadf0 are those two runtime objects. The hand-asm tells across the block, each measured over the whole ROM: `stmdb sp!` carrying r12 occurs at 39 sites, ALL inside ITCM (25 of them also carrying an argument register -- the caller-saved wrapper -- and 14 in otherwise ordinary prologues); zero of either shape in 640 KB of arm9 once the embedded ITCM image at file offset 0x97000 is excluded, and zero across all 103 overlays. Several members additionally have multiple entry points, statically unreachable instructions, or use the carry flag as a bidirectional data path, none of which C expresses. Two independent cold attempts on __aeabi_idiv and __aeabi_uidiv confirmed the class. See notes/itcm.md. Marked so schedulers stop offering 12.4 KB of vendor code as cold-match work: floor_set() is the only portable park (progress/nonmatching.jsonl is gitignored), so this record IS the routing exclusion. Remove the floor if a compiler build ever reproduces one of these. This symbol is an unreferenced argument-swap entry that falls through into the next function -- zero callers anywhere, entered only by fallthrough. It must stay adjacent to its successor, so it must NOT be carved into its own delink object.
